children: Shares of Palvella Therapeutics are trading higher after the U.S Food and Drug Administration granted priority review for Qtorin.

Palvella says Qtorin could become the first FDA-approved therapy for microcystic lymphatic malformations, a rare condition caused by a genetic mutation that result in cysts on the skin or in the mouth.
The company's stock was trading at $144.49, up 8.7%.
The FDA set a prescription drug user fee act target action date of Feb. 28. 2027, for Qtorin, also known as rapamycin.
The biopharmaceutical company said it is focused on developing and commercializing novel therapies for serious, rare skin diseases and vascular anomalies which have no FDA-approved therapies.
